title: RF-129 routing follow-ups from the #725 final review
acceptance: Refreshing on /classes/<id>/live fetches the run payload once, not twice (loadDetail, then getRunPayload).
Back/Forward to the class that is already selected switches the destination without refetching the class or reloading its detail.
A failed Apple sign-in that returns to /sign-in?error=... shows a plain-words error on the sign-in form.
Dashboard tests no longer rely on a setTimeout(0) wait for a queued jsdom history.back() between tests (stub it, or make the reset deterministic).
Decide whether stepTo's 'a return goes Back' design (pendingBack/selfPop) is worth its complexity, or replace it with plain pushes plus a Live-specific rule.
The legacy /?auth= redirect runs outside a useState initializer.

After a signed-out deep link, a sign-in that completes while signed in on / (not /sign-in) clears the remembered path, so a later /sign-in visit in that tab cannot jump to the old class (#725 final review at 2d358cd).

evidence.summary: Final review (/code-review medium) of 24ceeaf: one significant finding (stale return-to) fixed in #725; these six were logged as non-blocking.
Owner set RF-195 Ready for the Neo on 2026-11-04 ("Yes approved", quoted in this PR body); this draft PR is the Neo claim.
RF-129 set Done on a simulator check of production 840255c, which unblocks this task.
Dashboard URLs (RF-129): a refreshed /live path calls getRunPayload once; Back from Account to the open class makes no getClass, listClassTracks or getRunPayload call. Both failed before the fix.

Deep link forgotten once sign-in completes on /; /sign-in?error=invalid_code shows the plain-words Apple error and drops the code. Both failed before the fix. The /?auth= test calls redirectLegacyAuthIntent as main.tsx does. Final review of fe07411 found the code was stripped while the session check was pending (a real Apple failure is a fresh page load), so the message never showed; it is now stripped only once the check settles, and a test that starts pending failed before that fix.
settleAppRouteForTests waits for a queued stepTo Back, after which a new step pushes at once; redirectLegacyAuthIntent maps /?auth=signup and leaves other paths alone.
Login shows the Apple failure message when App passes the error code.

Deployed to production on 2026-11-07 from the Air: main f55b449a (#728, #744, #746, #745; records #743, #747), Worker 1d95a679-c9c3-4eb4-8371-980147c53a37, SPA assets/index-BVZTM4Zz.js, rollback ce487041-27d5-4edf-90e2-a6676522574e (75f09a1). No migrations. Smoke, headers and a 5-minute tail (0 exceptions) passed. Owner approval recorded before the deploy: https://github.com/steven-crosby/ritmofit-web/pull/746#issuecomment-6710041751. #728 for RF-195 is in that build. CI uses mock providers; this proves the deploy, not device behaviour.

resolution: All seven items met on #728 (Neo, 2026-11-06). (1) A refreshed /classes/<id>/live reuses the run payload the class detail read fetched: loadDetail returns it and restoreClass uses it, fetching again only when that read failed. (2) Back/Forward from another destination to the class still selected and loaded shows the class again, re-owning the detail workspace, with no getClass, track or payload read. (3) /sign-in?error=<code> shows one plain-words Apple sign-in error on the form (“Apple sign-in didn’t finish. Try again, or use your email.”, whatever the code), then drops the code from the URL once the session check has settled. One message, not a cancelled/failed split, kept the entry bundle under its 180 kB budget (179.98 kB). (4) Dashboard tests wait for a queued stepTo Back with settleAppRouteForTests, which resolves on that popstate, not on a setTimeout(0). (5) Decision (owner approved the default, 2026-11-06): keep stepTo’s return-goes-Back design. It is what keeps the browser Back and Forward a true record of the visit (an exit or close returns to the entry it came from instead of stacking a duplicate), its state is two flags in app-route.ts, and plain pushes would make Back after every close re-open the screen just left. (6) The legacy /?auth= redirect is redirectLegacyAuthIntent in app-route.ts, called once in main.tsx before the first render. (7) Signed in on any path but Sign in or Sign up clears the remembered return-to.
